title: 了 Step 1 · Done! Verb + 了
description: Verb + 了 says an action got done: 我买了三本书. Why it likes a number or a follow-up (了…就…), and why 我买了书。 sounds unfinished.

points.title: Verb + 了 = the action is done
points.summary: 了 straight after a verb says the action was completed.
points.body:
- 我买**了**三本书。 I bought three books.
- 他喝**了**两杯咖啡。 He drank two cups of coffee.
- 我们看**了**一个电影。 We watched a film.

Think of verb-了 as a tick ✔ next to the action.

**了 at a glance: done, or changed?**

| | where | means | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| verb-了 | right after the verb | **done** (completed action) | 我买**了**三本书。 |
| sentence-了 | end of the sentence | **changed** (new situation) | 下雨**了**。 我饿**了**。 |
| both | after the verb + at the end | **so far, and still going** | 我学**了**三年中文**了**。 |

**Where 了 does NOT go**
- With 没: 我**没**吃早饭 — never ~~没吃了~~.
- Habits and general states in the past: 我以前**常常**去, 他以前**是**老师, 我小时候**喜欢**画画.
- Plain description: 昨天很冷 — no 了 needed.

**Look-alikes:** 快 / 要 …了 = **about to** (快下雨了); 太…了 = **so / too** (太好了!) — no change involved.

points.title: It likes a number, a description — or a next step
points.summary: Verb-了 + a bare object sounds unfinished; add a number or description, or go on with the next action.
points.body:
- ✔ 我买了**三本**书。 / 我买了**很多**东西。
- 😐 我买了书。 — sounds like '…and then?'
- ✔ 我买了书**就**回家了。 (了…就… = as soon as / after doing X, …)
- ✔ 吃了饭**再**走吧。 (future: after eating, then go)

**了 at a glance: done, or changed?**

| | where | means | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| verb-了 | right after the verb | **done** (completed action) | 我买**了**三本书。 |
| sentence-了 | end of the sentence | **changed** (new situation) | 下雨**了**。 我饿**了**。 |
| both | after the verb + at the end | **so far, and still going** | 我学**了**三年中文**了**。 |

**Where 了 does NOT go**
- With 没: 我**没**吃早饭 — never ~~没吃了~~.
- Habits and general states in the past: 我以前**常常**去, 他以前**是**老师, 我小时候**喜欢**画画.
- Plain description: 昨天很冷 — no 了 needed.

**Look-alikes:** 快 / 要 …了 = **about to** (快下雨了); 太…了 = **so / too** (太好了!) — no change involved.
examples: I go home as soon as class is over.

notes: 着 = ongoing state — not a completed purchase.
的 doesn't go after a verb like this.

questions.prompt: What does 「{他|tā}{喝|hē}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{杯|bēi}{咖啡|kāfēi}。」 mean?
options: He drank two cups of coffee.
He's drinking two cups of coffee.
He drinks two cups of coffee (every day).
questions.translation: He drank two cups of coffee.

questions.prompt: Which sentence sounds **complete** on its own?
questions.explanation: Verb-了 likes a **number**: 买了三本书.
notes: One 了 at the end is enough here.
Verb-了 + a bare object sounds unfinished ('… and then?').

questions.explanation: **了…就…**: as soon as one action is done, the next follows.
notes: 才 = 'only then' — not the usual pattern here.
questions.translation: I go home as soon as class is over.

questions.prompt: {我们|wǒmen}{昨天|zuótiān}{看|kàn}（　）{一个|yí ge}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎokàn}{的|de}{电影|diànyǐng}。
questions.explanation: Done yesterday: 看**了**一个电影.
notes: 过了 doesn't fit a single film yesterday.
questions.translation: Yesterday we watched a really good film.

questions.prompt: Where does 了 go? 「{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}＿{两|liǎng}{碗|wǎn}＿{米饭|mǐfàn}＿。」
notes: 了 never comes before the verb.
了 goes right after the verb, not after the number.
questions.translation: I ate two bowls of rice.

questions.explanation: Verb-了 also works in the **future**: after you've eaten, then go.
notes: 的 doesn't follow a verb here.
questions.translation: Have something to eat before you go.

questions.prompt: 'I wrote three emails this morning.' Which sentence says so?
notes: Without 了 it sounds like a plan or a habit.
questions.translation: I wrote three emails this morning.

questions.prompt: What does 「{我|wǒ}{到|dào}{了|le}{北京|Běijīng}{就|jiù}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打|dǎ}{电话|diànhuà}。」 mean?
options: I called you when I was in Beijing.
I won't call you from Beijing.
I'll call you as soon as I get to Beijing.
questions.explanation: Verb-了 + **就** = as soon as (here in the future).
notes: 了…就… can be future: 'as soon as I've arrived'.
questions.translation: I'll call you as soon as I get to Beijing.
I drank three glasses of water.
